inputs: no physical optical hardware, laser, detector, or specimen (none exists in this repository)
negative_results: A REAL_DEVICE optical acquisition acquires NOTHING: OpticalRealDevice.acquire raises NoOpticalHardwareError and the physical run is PREREGISTERED_NOT_RUN; no laser, interferometer, photodetector, polarizer, or specimen exists here.

A photodiode is intensity-only and phase-blind: a surface displacement leaves the trace unchanged and is not recoverable from it; refuse_intensity_as_phase raises. Displacement is recoverable only from a phase-sensitive (interferometric or photoelastic) readout.

Each of the seven fault modes (clipping, drift, saturation, packet loss, missing samples, and the optical-specific fringe wash-out and speckle decorrelation) demonstrably alters the trace; fringe wash-out collapses fringe visibility and speckle decorrelation drops the correlation.
A reconstruction of a synthetic phantom/fringe is a SYNTHETIC_OBSERVATION, never an image of a real source: refuse_reconstruction_as_measured (delegating to r13.imaging) raises.

A synthetic observation is capped at evidence level E3 (calibrated self-test); it never reaches E4 (physical measurement) because the specimen, fixture, and raw physical artifact bindings are absent, and OpticalObservation refuses any measurement-class label.
No physical measurement was performed; measured_here is nothing and PHYSICAL_VALIDATION_NOT_CLAIMED.
reopening_test: Reopen the optical lane if: a REAL_DEVICE acquisition ever returns samples instead of raising NoOpticalHardwareError; a displacement is ever recovered from an intensity-only (photodiode) readout; a synthetic trace or reconstructed fringe is labelled a PHYSICAL_MEASUREMENT or an image of a real source; any synthetic observation reaches evidence level E4 or above; or a fault mode leaves the trace unchanged. The physical optical run is reopened only by a built, calibrated optical bench with a mounted specimen, a raw artifact, a clock binding, and an environment log.
